bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Mortgage Broker Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you are a mortgage broker or considering a career in mortgage broking, understanding how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential. Whether you are employed full-time, part-time, or casually, the formula is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This article explains the key components, including the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax, so you can estimate your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula for Annual Pay

For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the calculation is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your mortgage broker salary is based on an hourly rate of $30.00, your annual gross pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work part-time, simply replace 38 with your actual weekly hours. The same formula works for any employment type, but remember that casual employees receive a loading on top of the base rate.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. For the example above, weekly pay is $30.00 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates for Mortgage Brokers

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees must receive at least $33.05 per hour, which includes a 25% casual loading. However, the National Minimum Wage is a floor; most mortgage brokers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates.

Mortgage brokers may fall under awards such as the **Clerks – Private Sector Award** or the **Banking, Finance and Insurance Award**. These awards have specific classifications based on duties and experience, and their minimum rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, updated from 1 July 2026 with a 4.75% increase to award minimum wages. Always check the applicable award to ensure you are paid correctly.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual mortgage broker, your employer must pay a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave. Importantly, the casual loading is not the same as superannuation. **Superannuation guarantee** is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is calculated on your base rate plus any loadings, but not on overtime or allowances.

For example, if your base rate is $30.00 and you are casual, your hourly rate including loading is $30.00 × 1.25 = $37.50. Your super contribution would be 12% of your ordinary earnings (including the loading), so an additional $4.50 per hour, paid into your super fund.

## Estimating Take-Home Pay and Tax

Your annual gross pay is before tax and other deductions. For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Tax Office (ATO) resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% on the excess over $190,000

Additionally, the **Medicare levy** is generally 2% of your taxable income. Using the example of a $59,280 annual gross, your estimated tax would be approximately $8,244 (including Medicare), leaving a take-home pay of about $51,036 per year, or $981 per week. For a more precise estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

### Super Is Paid on Top

Remember that superannuation is not deducted from your gross pay; it is paid by your employer on top. So if your annual gross is $59,280, your employer also contributes $7,113.60 (12%) to your super fund, subject to the maximum contribution base. Your total remuneration package is therefore higher than your salary alone.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – use the checkbox to add it automatically. This tool is designed for employees covered by the National Minimum Wage or an award, and it assumes a consistent 38-hour week unless you adjust the hours.

### When Award Rates Differ

If your mortgage broker salary is governed by an award, the minimum hourly rate may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Clerks Award Level 3 rate from 1 July 2026 is approximately $27.50 per hour (check the latest [pay guides](/blog) for exact figures). Always use your award classification rate in the calculator for a more accurate estimate.

## Important Considerations

- **No unpaid overtime**: The formula assumes you are paid for every hour worked. If you work unpaid overtime, your effective hourly rate is lower.
- **No penalty rates or allowances**: Weekend, public holiday, or shift penalties are not included. These can significantly increase your pay.
- **No salary sacrifice**: The tax estimate uses the standard tax-free threshold. Salary packaging arrangements may reduce your taxable income.
- **HELP and MLS**: The calculator does not deduct HELP repayments or the Medicare levy surcharge. If you have a HELP debt or do not have appropriate private hospital cover, your take-home pay will be lower.

For a full breakdown of your mortgage broker salary, including award-specific rates, refer to the [reference tables](/data) on this site. They provide historical and current minimum wages, award classifications, and superannuation details.

## Conclusion

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary for a mortgage broker is simple: multiply by hours per week and 52. But the real picture includes award minimums, casual loading, super paid on top, and tax. Use the tools and guides on this site to ensure you are paid correctly and to plan your finances. Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, understanding these fundamentals puts you in control.
